title: The write step writes a T3 logo through its template style frame in the contract call, and the kit-logo-unsettable gate uses the same decision
steps: S1: From the repository root run: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/write-step-brand.test.mjs
S2: From the repository root run: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/template-kit-flow-reads.test.mjs
S3: Record the exit codes, the '# pass' and '# fail' lines and the result of each test named in run.tests.
expect: S1 and S2 exit 0 with '# fail 0'.

On a made-up T3 kit every logo spot that names a style param (logoimage) is a contract order on its templateStyle frame, the run never calls template.siteSettings and every logo line is written; a T4 kit keeps its profile, small-logo and contract orders; the gate holds Publish for a T3 spot whose frame the content map lacks and passes it when the map holds the frame.
evidence: JA Diner j6 1.0.5 kit: logo spot logo-header-1 has setting logoimage and frame templateStyle-9.0; the old logoOrder made it a profile order, which a T3 site cannot take, and the gate passed it because it named a setting. Measured: the three new tests fail on the old code and pass on the new one.
fence: Mechanism only: which path each logo order takes and what the gate decides. Not covered: a live write on a real T3 site, and the T3 favicon .ico.

tests: a T3 logo is a template style param: it goes in the contract call, never through the T4 site profile
on a T3 kit every logo is written by the one contract call and the site profile is never asked
kit-logo-unsettable: a T3 style param is no profile setting, so only its content map frame writes it
